title: Knowledge grounding: which data can a Copilot Studio agent answer from?
summary: Pass: Microsoft's documentation supports the controls, credit rates and knowledge-source restrictions described here. Add the Dataverse developer reference that explicitly connects the API property to the search setting.

claims.where: summary; What it is
claims.claim: Knowledge sources ground an agent's responses in enterprise content.
claims.quote: Knowledge sources ground your agent's responses in enterprise data.

claims.where: What it is; Why it matters
claims.claim: Makers choose the knowledge sources an agent can reference.
claims.quote: Makers can choose which types of knowledge sources their agents can reference.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Standard-harness agents can incorporate knowledge on the Knowledge page or in a generative answers node in a topic.
claims.quote: You can incorporate knowledge at the agent level, in the Knowledge page, or at the topic level, with a generative answers node in an agent topic.

claims.where: What it is
claims.claim: Published agents use their configured knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Published agents that contain knowledge use the configured knowledge sources to ground the published agent.

claims.where: What it is: authentication paragraph
claims.claim: Agent user authentication limits surfaced content to what the asking user can access.
claims.quote: Agent user authentication for knowledge sources means that when a specific user asks a question of the agent, the agent only surfaces content that the specific user can access.

claims.where: What it is: Dataverse prerequisites; controls[2].governs
claims.claim: Dataverse knowledge sources require Dataverse search in the environment.
claims.quote: To use this knowledge source, Copilot Studio agents must use Dataverse search.

claims.where: What it is: Dataverse prerequisites
claims.claim: A Dataverse knowledge source supports up to 15 tables.
claims.quote: You can add up to 15 Dataverse tables per knowledge source.

claims.where: What it is: Dataverse prerequisites
claims.claim: Dataverse knowledge sources require Authenticate with Microsoft.
claims.quote: Dataverse tables as knowledge sources require you to set your agent's authentication to Authenticate with Microsoft. The other two options, No authentication and Authenticate manually aren't currently supported.

claims.where: What it is: source filtering
claims.claim: Generative orchestration filters sources using an internal GPT model above 25 different knowledge sources.
claims.quote: Generative orchestration filters knowledge sources by using an internal GPT model when there are more than 25 different knowledge sources.

claims.where: What it is: source filtering
claims.claim: Uploaded files are excluded from the 25-source count.
claims.quote: Files uploaded to the agent aren't part of the 25 knowledge source search limit.

claims.where: What it is: A different sense
claims.claim: Work IQ enables agents to access Microsoft 365 and business data.
claims.quote: In addition to productivity data from Microsoft 365 applications, Work IQ also includes business and workflow data from Dynamics 365 and Power Platform, and data from connected enterprise systems through Copilot Connectors.

claims.where: Why it matters; Open questions: default
claims.claim: Microsoft's administrator-setting page does not state the default for Knowledge sources for agents.
claims.quote: Searched: "Knowledge sources for agents" "default state"; "Knowledge sources for agents" "default" "published". Read Configure knowledge sources for agents in the Power Platform admin center and Choose knowledge sources; no default stated.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risks and limits: Ungrounded answers; controls[3].governs
claims.claim: Allow ungrounded responses permits answers from general knowledge without using a source or tool.
claims.quote: When you turn on the Allow ungrounded responses setting, your agent can respond by using the model's general knowledge, even when it doesn't use any knowledge sources or tools.

claims.where: Why it matters: admin-centre setting
claims.claim: No admin-centre setting specifically for Allow ungrounded responses is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: "Allow ungrounded responses" "Power Platform admin center"; "Allow ungrounded responses" API PowerShell admin center. Read Knowledge sources summary and Orchestrate agent behavior with generative AI; only an agent setting was documented.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: billing scope
claims.claim: The cited Billing rates and management page describes standard-harness billing in Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: This article describes features used in agents or agent flows powered by the standard harness.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Classic answer rate
claims.claim: The standard-harness Classic answer rate is 1 Copilot Credit.
claims.quote: | Classic answer | 1 Copilot Credit | No charge |

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Generative answer rate
claims.claim: The standard-harness Generative answer rate is 2 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Generative answer^2^ | 2 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Tenant graph grounding rate
claims.claim: The standard-harness Tenant graph grounding for messages rate is 10 Copilot Credits.
claims.quote: | Tenant graph grounding for messages | 10 Copilot Credits | No charge |

claims.where: Cost and licensing: complex-prompt example
claims.claim: Microsoft's example uses 12 Copilot Credits for one tenant-graph-grounded complex prompt.
claims.quote: an agent grounded in a tenant graph could use 12 Copilot Credits (10 Copilot Credits for tenant graph grounding, and 2 Copilot Credits for generative answers) to respond to a single complex prompt from a user.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Microsoft Copilot harness
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing charges Copilot Credits for LLM tokens.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Microsoft Copilot harness
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing charges Copilot Credits for tools including knowledge and MCPs.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Microsoft Copilot harness
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness billing also charges for the harness itself.
claims.quote: Copilot Credits are charged for large language model (LLM) tokens, tools (including knowledge and MCPs), and the harness itself.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: employee-facing inclusion
claims.claim: The billing page includes employee-facing agent usage in the Microsoft Copilot USL when the user has that licence.
claims.quote: Employee-facing usage scenarios (Business to Employee) of Copilot Studio agents and Copilot Studio tools and features that these agents invoke are included in the Microsoft Copilot USL when the user of the agent is licensed with Microsoft Copilot

claims.where: Cost and licensing: employee-facing inclusion
claims.claim: The employee-facing inclusion requires operation under the authenticated licensed user's identity.
claims.quote: and the agent operates using the authenticated Microsoft Copilot USL user's identity.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: employee-facing inclusion
claims.claim: The employee-facing inclusion is subject to fair usage limits.
claims.quote: Usage is limited to fair usage limits.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: generative-answer charging footnote
claims.claim: The billing page says generative answers incur charges unless created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 without tenant graph grounding.
claims.quote: Agents incur charges for generative answer responses unless the agent is created in Agent Builder in Microsoft 365 and the response doesn't leverage tenant graph grounding.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: tenant graph option
claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding can be turned on or off for each agent.
claims.quote: This capability is optional, and you can turn it on or off for each agent.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: tenant graph default
claims.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed users use tenant graph grounding semantic search by default.
claims.quote: By default, all users with the Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses use tenant graph grounding semantic search.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: tenant graph cost; controls[4].governs
claims.claim: Enabling tenant graph grounding for users without Microsoft 365 Copilot licences adds cost.
claims.quote: if not all end users have Microsoft 365 Copilot licenses, turn on this setting to leverage semantic index for those users to improve quality. This feature comes at an extra cost.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: tenant graph prerequisites; controls[4].note
claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding requires a configured semantic index.
claims.quote: It also requires that a semantic index is configured for use.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: tenant graph prerequisites; controls[4].note
claims.claim: Using the semantic index requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot licence assigned to at least one user.
claims.quote: To use a semantic index, the Microsoft 365 Copilot license must be assigned to at least one user in the enterprise.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: tenant graph prerequisites; controls[4].note
claims.claim: The Microsoft 365 Copilot licence must be in the agent's tenant.
claims.quote: This feature requires the agent to share a tenant with a Microsoft 365 Copilot license.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: SharePoint uploads
claims.claim: Files added through Upload files > SharePoint are stored in Dataverse.
claims.quote: When you use Upload files > SharePoint as a knowledge source, your files are stored in Dataverse, where they're processed and indexed for use.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: SharePoint uploads
claims.claim: SharePoint-upload files and folders consume Dataverse data storage.
claims.quote: Your files and folders remain in Dataverse, so they do consume data storage.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Ungrounded answers stay possible
claims.claim: Turning off Allow ungrounded responses does not prevent combining general knowledge with retrieved content.
claims.quote: The agent's underlying model might still incorporate general knowledge when it combines this knowledge with information it retrieves from knowledge sources or tools.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: With Allow ungrounded responses off, a response is blocked if no knowledge source or tool was used during the turn.
claims.quote: When you turn off this setting, the agent blocks any response generated in a turn where it didn't use a knowledge source or tool.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: A follow-up answered only from conversation history can be blocked.
claims.quote: This condition means the response is blocked if the agent answers a question from conversation history or general knowledge without calling a knowledge source or tool.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: With the setting off, returning an answer from a knowledge source requires an in-text citation.
claims.quote: When you turn off Allow ungrounded responses, the agent returns an answer from a knowledge source only when the answer includes an in-text citation to that source.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning it off withholds answers
claims.claim: A correct answer from a source can be withheld when it lacks a citation.
claims.quote: Occasionally, the model generates a correct answer from a knowledge source but doesn't include a citation for it. When that happens, the agent withholds the answer and responds as though it didn't find any information.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The Documents setting is narrow
claims.claim: Disallowing Documents uploads blocks only local file uploads.
claims.quote: Configuring Documents knowledge source to not allow uploads only prevents local file uploads.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The Documents setting is narrow
claims.claim: Preventing SharePoint and OneDrive uploads also requires restricting SharePoint + OneDrive.
claims.quote: It doesn't prevent makers from adding files from SharePoint or OneDrive. To not allow uploads from SharePoint or OneDrive, configure SharePoint + OneDrive to not allow access.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Uploaded files skip per-user checks
claims.claim: The upload files method lets anyone with permission to the agent access the file.
claims.quote: The upload files method allows anyone with permission to the agent to access the file.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Uploaded files skip per-user checks
claims.claim: SharePoint verifies the user's credentials and file permissions before providing responses.
claims.quote: With SharePoint, the user's credentials are verified to ensure they have permission to access the file before providing responses.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Dataverse search off; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft documents index deprovisioning and removal within 12 hours after turning off Dataverse search.
claims.quote: Turning off Dataverse search deprovisions and removes the index within 12 hours.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Dataverse search off; controls[2].governs
claims.claim: Turning off Dataverse search stops agent experiences relying on uploaded files.
claims.quote: The agent doesn't provide results that rely on this indexed data until Dataverse search is enabled for the environment. The agent uses the fallback answer by default.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Dataverse search off
claims.claim: Turning off Dataverse search stops agent experiences relying on SharePoint or OneDrive files added via upload.
claims.quote: any generative AI experience that relies on Dataverse, like uploaded files or using OneDrive or SharePoint files (via upload) in Microsoft Copilot Studio agents, among other experiences.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Dataverse search off
claims.claim: Rebuilding the index after it was removed can take an hour or more for average-sized organisations.
claims.quote: If you turn on Dataverse search after it's been off for 12 hours, it creates a fresh index that needs to go through a full sync. Syncing can take an hour or more for average size organizations, and a couple of days for large organizations.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Dataverse search off
claims.claim: Index rebuilding can take a couple of days for large organisations.
claims.quote: Syncing can take an hour or more for average size organizations, and a couple of days for large organizations.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Turning Dataverse search off; What to check
claims.claim: Microsoft also cautions that index removal or provisioning can take multiple days depending on indexed volume.
claims.quote: Index removal (or provisioning) can take multiple days to be completed, depending on the amount of Dataverse search consumption.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Web search reaches beyond your list
claims.claim: Standard-harness web search searches all public websites indexed by Bing when triggered.
claims.quote: It searches all public websites indexed by Bing.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Web search reaches beyond your list
claims.claim: Standard-harness web search runs in parallel with configured public website source searches.
claims.quote: This type of search happens in parallel with any searches of public websites you added as knowledge sources.

claims.where: Risks and limits: Web search reaches beyond your list
claims.claim: Microsoft Copilot harness agents retain existing website sources but do not use them while web search is on.
claims.quote: Websites you already added are kept but aren't used until you turn web search off.

claims.where: Risks and limits: The tenant graph option needs sign-in; controls[4].note
claims.claim: Tenant graph grounding requires Authenticate with Microsoft.
claims.quote: The Tenant graph grounding with semantic search feature requires that the agent's user authentication is set to Authenticate with Microsoft.
